item.title: Why Do Expensive Products Get Worse Ratings?
item.description: Motivation Several years ago, I was looking for speakers on Amazon. Prices varied widely, from $25 to $250 or more. As I browsed, I noticed an interesting pattern: the most expensive speakers had the lowest average rating. More recently, I discovered the study “Expensive Running Shoes Are Not Better Than More Affordable Running Shoes.” The study finds that shoes with higher prices tended to get lower ratings. The 10 most expensive shoes in the study had an average cost of $191 and an average rating of 79, while the 10 cheapest had an average cost of $60 and an average rating of 86.
